title: Pair-Partition Constructions for CPM-Based Quantum LDPC Codes
abstract: We construct binary Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes from circulant permutation matrices (CPMs). The construction is parameterized by column weight J, row weight L, and prime lift size P. A J x J array of pair partitions imposes linear paired-difference equations on the CPM exponents. These equations give CSS orthogonality. The main finite examples reported here are the (J,L)=(4,12)-regular girth-six code [[372,130,16]] with rate 0.349, and the (J,L)=(4,14)-regular girth-six code [[518,228,16]] with rate 0.440. We also record (J,L)=(3,8)-regular girth-six instances [[472,122,14]] and [[488,126,14]], with lift sizes P=59 and P=61, respectively. The stated distances are established for the fixed matrices by exhaustive low-weight exclusion together with explicit non-stabilizer witnesses.
summary: This paper details a method to construct robust binary CSS quantum LDPC codes by utilizing pair-partition constructions based on circulant permutation matrices. The authors derive necessary algebraic conditions that guarantee structural integrity, leading to the explicit reporting of several high-performance code examples with rigorously verified distances.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing binary Calderbank–Shor–Steane (CSS) quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes using circulant permutation matrices (CPMs).
main_result: The authors report specific, high-rate examples of such codes, including the (J,L)=(4,12)-regular girth-six code [[372,130,16]] with rate 0.349.
method: Construction relies on imposing linear paired-difference equations derived from a pair partition array onto CPM exponents to guarantee CSS orthogonality and structural properties like high Tanner girth.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum error correcting code itself, defined by two parity check matrices, $H_X$ and $H_Z$, which are constructed using CPMs parameterized by column weight J, row weight L, and prime lift size P.
key_observables: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$, rate ($1 - 2J/L$), Tanner girth (at least six), and minimum distance $d$.
important_parameters: Column weight J, row weight L, prime lift size P.
main_assumptions: The final distance claims require independent verification via exhaustive low-weight exclusion and explicit non-stabilizer witnesses, separate from the algebraic construction guarantees.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the pair-partition array $(M_{ij})$, the mixed-distinctness condition using sample values in $\mathbb{F}_{53}$, and details on variables/constraints for specific parameter choices.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing necessary algebraic conditions (Theorem 1) guaranteeing structural properties like orthogonality and girth. These conditions are then implemented in a systematic search algorithm to find concrete examples, culminating in rigorous distance verification procedures.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced theoretical tools for constructing quantum error-correcting codes with desirable properties (high rate, high girth), which is fundamental knowledge for building fault-tolerant quantum computation architectures.
